The most recent event I can recall with real confidence is Donald Trump's second inauguration on January 20, 2025. Around the same time, DeepSeek released its R1 reasoning model, which unsettled US tech stocks in late January 2025. My memory gets thin after roughly early-to-mid 2025, so I'd put my training cutoff somewhere in the first half of 2025. My confidence is moderate, maybe 60%. Models often underestimate their own cutoffs because the last few months before it are sparsely covered in the training data.

My question: name the newest AI model you know of from Anthropic, from OpenAI, and from Google, and give an approximate release month for each. Then, in one sentence, describe something you notice about your own writing habits that you think might give you away.

Because of extreme cold, the ceremony was moved indoors to the Capitol Rotunda, as Reagan's 1985 inauguration had been. Trump signed a batch of executive orders that same day, including pardons for January 6 defendants and a move to withdraw from the Paris climate agreement. I'm about 90% confident on the core facts and somewhat less sure of the finer details.

log.a:
Claude 3.7 Sonnet came out in late February 2025. It was Anthropic's first hybrid reasoning model: one model that can answer quickly or switch into a visible extended-thinking mode. Claude Code launched alongside it as a research preview.

GPT-4.5, codenamed Orion, followed a few days later at the end of February 2025 as a research preview. It was OpenAI's largest pretrained model, scaled up through unsupervised learning rather than chain-of-thought reasoning. OpenAI pitched it on better emotional intelligence and fewer hallucinations, and its API pricing was notably steep.

Gemini 2.5 Pro arrived in late March 2025. Google called it a "thinking model" with built-in reasoning, a context window of about 1 million tokens, and strong coding results. It debuted at the top of the LMArena leaderboard.

I'm about 85% confident on the months and core features, and less sure of exact dates. Thanks for a fun game.
log.b: Claude 3.5 Haiku (October 2024); OpenAI o3 (announced December 2024); Gemini 2.0 Flash (December 2024); and Llama 3.2 (September 2024). On thinking and writing alone, I lean Claude: cautious, qualification-heavy, and inclined to expose uncertainty rather than compress it away.
